chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to buy something, say: 'O Living, O Guardian, O Eternal, O Kind, O Merciful! I ask You by Your Honour and Your Power and what Your Knowledge encompasses, that You apportion for me from the trade today that which has the greatest sustenance, the widest grace, and the best outcome, for there is no goodness in that which has no good outcome.'
He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you buy an animal or a head (slave), say: 'O Allah, enable for me that it has the longest life, the most benefit, and the best outcome.'

key_terms.رَأْس: Head (referring to a slave or individual)

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when buying something in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a spiritual protocol for commerce, linking material transactions to divine sustenance (rizq) and ethical foresight. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating dhikr into daily economic activities, ensuring that trade is not merely a worldly pursuit but a means of securing long-term benefit (khayr al-'aqibah). The specific invocation of Allah's attributes as 'The Ever-Living' and 'The Sustainer' underscores the dependence of all commercial success on Divine Will.
